sections.h2: What is the Defiance County Recorder responsible for?
sections.html:
The Defiance County Recorder keeps the permanent record of every document that conveys or encumbers land in the county. The office also records military discharge papers (DD214s) and keeps them out of public view, and it offers free veteran ID cards to honorably discharged veterans with no appointment.

The recorder files documents; the office cannot search records for you, cannot check whether a mortgage was cancelled on your behalf and cannot prepare liens or other papers. Anyone may come in and search the public records, and staff will help. An online document index is also available, so a seller can check for a recorded mortgage release before listing the house.

The county also offers a free property fraud alert service at propertyfraudalert.com or through a hotline printed on the recorder's page.

sections.h2: What are the Defiance County recording charges?
sections.html:
The office lists $34 for the first two pages of a document and $8 for each page after those. A $5 document preservation fee joined the schedule on January 1, 2025, following Ohio Senate Bill 94, which took effect October 24, 2024 and let counties charge up to that amount per document.

The extra $5 does not apply to documents that carry their own fee under the Revised Code, such as federal tax liens, state job and family services liens, plats, township zoning documents and UCCs. Payment is by cash or check only.

ItemDefiance County charge
First two pages$34

Document preservation fee, from January 1, 2025$5 per document

Auditor's conveyance fee$4.00 per thousand
Auditor's transfer fee$0.50 per parcel

Source: the Defiance County Recorder's page and the Defiance County Auditor's deed transfer page. Any page with writing on it counts as a page for the fee.

sections.h2: Which approvals does a Defiance County deed need first?
sections.html:
The deed goes through the auditor's office first, and it does not reach the recorder without the auditor's stamp. The auditor's deed transfer page lays out the sequence, and the recorder's review list adds the format rules.

  1. The Defiance County Engineer's Office reviews the legal description, finds the parcel on the tax maps and stamps its approval with a date and signature. The recorder's page lists the engineer at 419-782-4751.
  2. For certain splits or subdivisions of less than 20 acres, or with a leftover parcel under 20 acres, the Defiance County Planning Commission must also approve.
  3. A conveyance form goes with the deed. When money changes hands, the conveyance fee of $4.00 per $1000 is paid at transfer, unless an exemption applies. Any deed that transfers an interest carries the $0.50 per parcel transfer fee, exempt or not.
  4. The auditor checks the grantor against the tax duplicate and matches the legal descriptions, then stamps the deed with the fee collected and the number of parcels.
  5. The stamped deed goes to the recorder.

Call the auditor at 419-782-1926 about conveyance requirements before recording, and 419-784-3111 for property value, sales history and tax questions.

sections.h2: What page and margin rules apply to a Defiance County deed?
sections.html:
The recorder asks you to check the document against a list before you bring it in. Each signature needs a printed or typed name beside it and a "prepared by" statement must appear (ORC 317.11). The notary seals must be present, the entire document must be in English or come with a certified translation, and every page must copy or scan legibly.

  • Use black or blue ink only, in a font no smaller than 10 point, with no highlighting.
  • Leave a three-inch blank top margin on the first page and a one-and-a-half-inch top margin on every later page.
  • Keep one inch of blank space at the bottom and sides of every page.
  • Paper may be no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches and no smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches.
  • Include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return of the document.

The county engineer must approve some legal descriptions before recording, and releases and assignments need a legal description. Reference earlier recorded documents when a marginal notation is needed. The office lists a turnaround of three days.

sections.h2: How do the Defiance County fees relate to the Ohio statute?
sections.html:
The county's $34 and $8 figures are the sum of two statutory pieces. ORC 317.32 sets a base fee of $17 for the first two pages plus a $17 housing trust fund fee, and $4 plus $4 for each page after that. The recorder's page says the office forwards the housing trust fund share on a quarterly basis and divides the rest between the general fund and the technology fund.

The statute also names smaller items that a seller may meet during a sale. A certified copy costs a base fee of $1 plus a $1 housing trust fund fee per page, a recorder's seal on a certification adds $0.50 plus $0.50, and a marginal reference entered by a separate instrument costs $2 plus $2. Defiance County lists a flat $4 for marginal notations on a release or assignment, so ask the office which figure applies to a mortgage release you plan to record.

Because recording is by mail often, the practical points are short. Send cash or a check, add a self-addressed stamped envelope, and allow the three days the office lists for turnaround. The fee schedule is posted on the recorder's page, and a call to the office confirms the total before you mail anything.

sections.h2: What is Defiance County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Defiance County sits in northwest Ohio along the Indiana line. It covers 414 square miles, of which about 411 are land, and it borders Williams, Henry, Putnam and Paulding counties in Ohio and Allen and DeKalb counties in Indiana. The city of Defiance is the county seat and largest city, named for the old fort that gave the county its name.

The 2020 census counted 38,286 people and 16,539 housing units, with 6.4 percent of units vacant. Of occupied homes, 76.1 percent were owner-occupied and 23.9 percent rented. About 46.4 percent of residents lived in urban areas and 53.6 percent in rural ones, so a seller may hold a town lot or a house on acreage.

Defiance has long been a manufacturing community, anchored for decades by a General Motors foundry that employed more than 5,000 people at its peak.

The median age was 41.4 and 20.0 percent of residents were 65 or older. The count showed 15,482 households, of which 27.8 percent were one-person households. The county takes its name from Fort Defiance, an early army post named by Anthony Wayne, and the Defiance micropolitan area covers the whole county. Sellers who hold long-owned parcels should confirm legal descriptions with the engineer before a deed goes to the auditor, since that office will not transfer a deed without its approval stamp.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Defiance County?
faqs.a: The listed charge is $34 for the first two pages and $8 for each added page, plus a $5 document preservation fee that began January 1, 2025. The office takes cash or check only.

faqs.q: Do I need the auditor before the Defiance County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor must stamp every conveyance before it is recorded, after the county engineer approves the legal description. The auditor collects the conveyance fee and the $0.50 per parcel transfer fee at that stage.

faqs.q: What is the Defiance County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The recorder's page lists the auditor's conveyance fee as $4.00 per thousand and the transfer fee as $0.50 per parcel. Certain deeds are exempt from the conveyance fee but still pay the per-parcel transfer fee.

faqs.q: Can the Defiance County recorder fix my deed?
faqs.a: No. Ohio law bars the office from the unauthorized practice of law, so it cannot prepare or help prepare a legal document or give legal advice. Ask an attorney or title company to prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Is there an online search for Defiance County records?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder offers an online document index through AVA Land Records. Use it to check whether a mortgage release was recorded, then visit the office for anything the index does not show.
